newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile inflation no cause for concern-cenbank gov.
newsitem.headline: Chile inflation no cause for concern-cenbank gov.

text.p: Chile's Central Bank is not worried that inflation is picking up after February's higher-than-expected rise in consumer prices, said president Carlos Massad.
"We are not concerned. We believe that this year we are in perfect conditions to meet the inflation target of 5.5 percent," Massad told reporters.

Consumer prices increased 0.8 percent in February, compared with 0.5 percent in the same month last year. The figure brought the inflation rate to 7.2 percent over the last 12 months and to 1.3 percent in the first two months of the year.
The bank is pleased with progress made in cooling Chile's strong economic growth which had last year threatened to fuel inflation, he said.
"We are very satisfied, apart from the unpleasant surprise we had in February which was for purely one-off reasons," said Massad.
February's inflation rate was skewed by this year's drought which pushed up food prices.
The authorities aim to bring Chile's growth rate down to 5.5 percent from around seven percent last year.
